extraction.name: Geometry3K
extraction.description: A large-scale benchmark consisting of 3,002 geometry problems with dense annotation in formal language. The dataset includes SAT-style problems collected from two high-school textbooks covering diverse geometric shapes and problem goals.
extraction.creator: Pan Lu, Ran Gong, Shibiao Jiang, Liang Qiu, Siyuan Huang, Xiaodan Liang, Song-Chun Zhu
extraction.citeAs: Inter-GPS: Interpretable Geometry Problem Solving with Formal Language and Symbolic Reasoning. Pan Lu, Ran Gong, Shibiao Jiang, Liang Qiu, Siyuan Huang, Xiaodan Liang, Song-Chun Zhu. arXiv:2105.04165v3 [cs.CL] 20 Jul 2021
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The data is collected from two popular textbooks for high school students across grades 6-12 by two online digital libraries (McGraw-Hill, Geometryonline). Groups of well-trained annotators with undergraduate degrees manually collect each problem with its problem text, geometry diagram, four candidate choices, and correct answer.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Two popular textbooks for high school students across grades 6-12 from two online digital libraries (McGraw-Hill, Geometryonline)
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Each problem in Geometry3K is annotated with dense descriptions in formal language. Each problem data is labeled with the corresponding problem goal and geometry shapes. The annotated formal language is used to train and evaluate the proposed problem parsers.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Groups of well-trained annotators with undergraduate degrees
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is divided into train, validation, and test sets with the ratio of 0.7:0.1:0.2. The Geometry3K dataset consists of 2,101 training data, 300 validation data, and 601 test data. The dataset is used for training and evaluating geometry problem solving algorithms.
